payload.description:
**Follow-on under `PPY-54055d`.** Diagnose already fuses heuristics, profile `rules:`, and 4-gram redundancy. This slice adds a **quantitative density / concept-restatement** signal so long fluff (one idea restated many times) is a steer-able red flag.

## Intent

As a publication operator, I want diagnose to report how thinly information is spread — including the same concept said in different words — so I can mark those passages rewrite/delete instead of publishing a long article that could be a paragraph.

## Why embeddings (local only)

4-word shingles miss paraphrase. Local sentence embeddings (or TF-IDF cosine as fallback) cluster sentences by meaning. **Cluster count is a proxy for distinct claims**, not a true ontology. Numbers stay advisory; they are not an AI-detector and not a score to game.

Paid vector APIs are forbidden here. Do **not** call OpenAI or `papyrus_knowledge_query` embeddings.

## Fusion model

Keep independent signals. Do **not** collapse into one weighted “fluff score.”

1. Existing findings (lead-ins, rules, 4-gram redundancy, …) unchanged.
2. New top-level `density` summary (always present when the check is on): word/sentence counts, cluster count, sentences-per-cluster, largest-cluster share, gzip ratio, embedder id.
3. New steer-able findings when thresholds in the style profile are crossed:
   - document-level `low_information_density` when the draft is long enough and sentences-per-cluster is above the cap
   - `concept_restatement` groups (same shape as `repetition_groups`) when a semantic cluster has enough sentences that are **not** already a 4-gram redundancy group

An operator/LLM steers those findings like any other. Prefer deletion in later option generation; this story does not rewrite.

## Done when

- Style profile may include `checks.informationDensity` (default on) and optional `density:` thresholds (`minWords`, `maxSentencesPerCluster`, `restatementMinSentences`, `cosineThreshold`, `embedder`: `local` | `tfidf` | `off`).
- Diagnose JSON includes `density` with the numbers above. `embedder` is a local model id, `tfidf`, or `off` — never an API vendor name.
- A fixture that restates one claim three times in different wording (no shared 4-gram) produces a `concept_restatement` group. 4-gram redundancy alone must not be the only way that fixture is caught.
- A long synthetic fluff draft (high sentence count, few clusters) produces `low_information_density`. A must-pass Anth.us reference excerpt above `minWords` does not.
- Short drafts below `minWords` do not get `low_information_density`.
- Local embedder is optional at install time (Poetry extra or equivalent). If it is missing, TF-IDF cosine clustering still runs and `density.embedder` is `tfidf`. Tests inject vectors or use TF-IDF so CI does not download a model.
- Detector-score keys remain forbidden. gzip/lexical/embedding stats are editorial density, not “AI probability.”

## Out of scope

Rewrite options (PPY-73906c). Verifier scoring (PPY-5ca22f) may consume `density` later; do not build the verifier. Newsroom UI. Remote embedding APIs. Topic models / LLM-as-judge for concept count.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Diagnose information density and concept restatement
  As a publication operator
  I want density numbers and restatement clusters in diagnose JSON
  So I can steer long fluff and paraphrased repeats without an LLM in this pass

  Scenario: Density summary is present
    Given a loadable style profile with information density enabled
    And a draft of several sentences
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then the JSON includes density with wordCount, sentenceCount, clusterCount, sentencesPerCluster, gzipRatio, and embedder
    And embedder is not a paid API name

  Scenario: Three paraphrases of one claim are clustered
    Given a draft that states the same claim three times in different words with no repeated four-word phrase
    And a loadable style profile
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is a concept_restatement group with at least three member sentences
    And that group is not justified only by four-word shingles

  Scenario: Long fluff is low density
    Given a draft longer than the profile minWords that restates few claims across many sentences
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is a low_information_density finding

  Scenario: House-voice excerpt is not flagged as fluff
    Given a must-pass excerpt from an Anth.us reference sample longer than minWords
    And the Anth.us style profile
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no low_information_density finding

  Scenario: Short drafts skip the document-level density flag
    Given a draft shorter than the profile minWords
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no low_information_density finding
```
payload.title: Information density and concept-restatement signals
